observations: Photo 0 shows a Nikon D750 retail box with a USPS Ground Advantage shipping label attached.
Photo 0 also shows a Nikkor 50mm lens box and a Zhiyun gimbal box in the background.
Photo 1 shows the D750 box open, containing two user manuals (one in English, one in French).
Photo 2 shows the interior of the box with two items wrapped in bubble wrap; the camera body itself is not visible.
The seller's text specifies 'D750 Body' but the photos do not show the actual device.

claims.evidence: The USPS label in photo 0 suggests the box was shipped within or from the US, but this does not prove the camera's usage history.
The box and manuals for a D750 are shown, but the camera body itself is hidden in bubble wrap in photo 2.
The camera body is not visible and cannot be inspected for cosmetic condition.
There is no photo of the camera powered on or any proof of functionality.

risks.risk: The item inside the bubble wrap may not be a Nikon D750 or may be a different, lower-value model.
risks.proof: A photo of the camera body showing the 'D750' model badge.
risks.if_unproven: as the cheapest Nikon DSLR available

risks.risk: The camera body may have significant cosmetic damage, wear, or missing parts.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the camera body from the front, back, top, and bottom.

risks.risk: The image sensor may be scratched, dirty, or affected by fungus.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the sensor with the body cap removed.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a professional sensor replacement

risks.risk: The camera may be non-functional or have an extremely high shutter count.
risks.proof: A video of the camera powering on and taking a photo, plus a screenshot of the shutter count.

proof_requests: Photos of the actual camera body from all sides, removed from the bubble wrap.
A photo of the camera sensor with the body cap removed.
A photo of the camera screen turned on showing the menu.
A screenshot or photo showing the current shutter count.
response.reason: The seller has only provided photos of the packaging and manuals. The camera body itself is completely obscured by bubble wrap in the only photo of the box's interior, making it impossible to verify the item's identity, condition, or presence.
